title: Noor and the Letter
premise: In 1852, mapmaker's apprentice Cyrus Blackwood is secretly completing the atlas his master died charting when a stranger named Noor arrives bearing a letter in the master's unmistakable hand — proof the old man faked his death and is alive, hunted, and hiding. The letter leads Cyrus and Noor across coastal ports and forged charts to a smugglers' berth on the last ship out before the authorities close the net. When only one berth remains, Cyrus must choose between Noor, who has become the family he never had, and the master he loved like a father. He gives the berth to Noor, stays behind to burn the atlas and face the inquest himself, and in the final chapter, years later as a master mapmaker in his own right, receives a letter in Noor's handwriting — alive, returned, home.
about_author: I. M. Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime charts in a coastal library before turning to fiction. They write historical novels about the quiet, stubborn people history forgets to record.
